covers: INT 33h, the mouse driver: every function the emulator's INT33_Handler has a case for.

entries.name: reset driver
entries.description: Resets the mouse driver and reports whether it is installed and how many buttons it has.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=FFFFh, BX=3 and reinitialises the driver: cursor hidden, ranges and cursor shapes back to video-mode defaults, pointer centred, counters and call mask cleared. With the built-in driver switched off (MOUSE /U) AX and BX stay as passed and nothing resets. INT 33h is not installed when the mouse type is none (no serial mouse) or int33 is off.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE - RESET DRIVER AND READ STATUS
case 0x00:  /* MS MOUSE - RESET DRIVER AND READ STATUS */

entries.name: show cursor
entries.description: Shows the mouse cursor by decrementing its hide counter.
entries.behaviour: Decrements the hide counter if it is above 0 and draws the cursor when it reaches 0; a reset leaves it at 1. Also clears the update region of AX=0010h, changes no register, and draws nothing in a video mode the mouse code does not know. On PC-98 NEC mouse mode the counter is forced to 0.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - SHOW MOUSE CURSOR
case 0x01:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - SHOW MOUSE CURSOR */

entries.name: hide cursor
entries.description: Hides the mouse cursor by incrementing its hide counter.
entries.behaviour: Restores the screen under the cursor and increments the hide counter, so each hide needs one AX=0001h. No register changes. With the host cursor in use and the mouse not captured it also hides the host cursor.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - HIDE MOUSE CURSOR
case 0x02:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - HIDE MOUSE CURSOR */

entries.name: position and buttons
entries.description: Returns the cursor position and the state of the mouse buttons.
entries.behaviour: BL=buttons (1 left, 2 right, 4 middle), BH=wheel movement since the last read as a signed byte (CuteMouse extension, then cleared), CX=x, DX=y; AX unchanged. Text modes give multiples of 8 (x of modes 0 and 1: 16), modes 0Dh and 13h give even x. PC-98 NEC mode: AX=FFFFh if left, BX=FFFFh if right pressed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN POSITION AND BUTTON STATUS
case 0x03:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN POSITION AND BUTTON STATUS */

entries.name: set cursor position
entries.description: Moves the mouse cursor to the given column and row.
entries.behaviour: CX=x, DX=y. A value at or beyond the range edge becomes that edge; otherwise a coordinate is replaced only if it differs from the reported one, so a rounded value does not overwrite the exact one. Redraws the cursor and changes no register.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - POSITION MOUSE CURSOR
case 0x04:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - POSITION MOUSE CURSOR */

entries.name: button press data
entries.description: Returns the press count and last press position of one mouse button.
entries.behaviour: BX=button, above 2 treated as 2; returns AX=button bits, BX=presses since the last call (then zeroed), CX,DX=position of the last press. BX=FFFFh asks for the wheel (CuteMouse): BX=wheel count, low 8 bits only, then cleared, CX,DX=last wheel position, AX unchanged. PC-98 NEC mode: left button only.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN BUTTON PRESS DATA
case 0x05:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN BUTTON PRESS DATA */

entries.name: button release data
entries.description: Returns the release count and last release position of one mouse button.
entries.behaviour: BX=button, above 2 treated as 2; returns AX=button bits, BX=releases since the last call (then zeroed), CX,DX=position of the last release. BX=FFFFh asks for the wheel (CuteMouse): BX=full 16-bit wheel count, then cleared, CX,DX=last wheel position, AX unchanged. PC-98 NEC mode: left button only.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN BUTTON RELEASE DATA
case 0x06:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - RETURN BUTTON RELEASE DATA */

entries.name: horizontal range
entries.description: Sets the minimum and maximum horizontal cursor position.
entries.behaviour: CX,DX=signed limits, swapped if CX is larger; the pointer is clamped into them. With no button down, or on the first call after a mode set, a range from 0 also sets the screen width for host-pointer mapping, rounded to the mode's width within 32 unless int33 max x is set. PC-98 NEC mode: right button press data.
entries.differs: The list says text-mode limits are truncated to cell multiples; the emulator stores them as given and masks only the coordinates it reports.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE HORIZONTAL CURSOR RANGE
case 0x07:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE HORIZONTAL CURSOR RANGE */

entries.name: vertical range
entries.description: Sets the minimum and maximum vertical cursor position.
entries.behaviour: CX,DX=signed limits, swapped if CX is larger; the pointer is clamped into them. With no button down, or on the first call after a mode set, a range from 0 also sets the screen height for host-pointer mapping, rounded to the mode's height within 32 unless int33 max y is set. PC-98 NEC mode: right button release data.
entries.differs: The list says text-mode limits are truncated to cell multiples; the emulator stores them as given and masks only the coordinates it reports.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE VERTICAL CURSOR RANGE
case 0x08:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE VERTICAL CURSOR RANGE */

entries.name: define graphics cursor
entries.description: Defines the shape and hot spot of the graphics-mode cursor.
entries.behaviour: ES:DX points to 16 screen-mask words then 16 cursor-mask words; BX,CX=hot spot column and row (signed words, unchecked). Sets cursor type 2 even in text mode, where it then draws as a software text cursor, and redraws. PC-98 NEC mode: reads 32 big-endian words into the cursor mask only.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v3.0+ - DEFINE GRAPHICS CURSOR
case 0x09:  /* MS MOUSE v3.0+ - DEFINE GRAPHICS CURSOR */

entries.name: define text cursor
entries.description: Selects the software or hardware text cursor and its masks or scan lines.
entries.behaviour: BX=0 selects the software cursor: character and attribute are ANDed with CX then XORed with DX. Any nonzero BX selects the hardware cursor with scan lines CL to DL. CX and DX are kept either way, graphics modes ignore them, and no register changes.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v3.0+ - DEFINE TEXT CURSOR
case 0x0a:  /* MS MOUSE v3.0+ - DEFINE TEXT CURSOR */

entries.name: read motion counters
entries.description: Returns the mouse motion in mickeys since the previous call.
entries.behaviour: CX=horizontal and DX=vertical mickeys as signed words, then both counters are cleared. Both are 0 while the host mouse is not captured by the window, because mickeys accumulate only then.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - READ MOTION COUNTERS
case 0x0b:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - READ MOTION COUNTERS */

entries.name: set event handler
entries.description: Installs a routine the driver calls on the events chosen by a call mask.
entries.behaviour: CX=call mask, ES:DX=routine, stored unchecked; a zero mask stops calls. The routine runs from the mouse IRQ in real or V86 mode, with AX=event bit, BL=buttons, BH=wheel byte, CX,DX=position, SI,DI=horizontal and vertical mickeys. Reset clears the mask.
entries.differs: The list has mask bits 7 to 15 unused; the emulator also uses bit 7 for wheel motion and, when mask bit 8 is set and the host mouse is not captured, sets bit 8 (absolute) in AX.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE INTERRUPT SUBROUTINE PARAMETERS
case 0x0c:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE INTERRUPT SUBROUTINE PARAMETERS */

entries.name: light pen on
entries.description: Turns on light pen emulation.
entries.behaviour: Does nothing: the emulator logs that light pen emulation is not implemented and changes no register.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - LIGHT PEN EMULATION ON
case 0x0d:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - LIGHT PEN EMULATION ON */

entries.name: light pen off
entries.description: Turns off light pen emulation.
entries.behaviour: Does nothing: the emulator logs that light pen emulation is not implemented and changes no register.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - LIGHT PEN EMULATION OFF
case 0x0e:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - LIGHT PEN EMULATION OFF */

entries.name: mickey pixel ratio
entries.description: Sets how many mickeys the mouse must move per 8 pixels of cursor motion.
entries.behaviour: CX=horizontal and DX=vertical mickeys per 8 pixels, signed words; the call is ignored if either is 0. A reset sets 8 and 16. No register changes.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE MICKEY/PIXEL RATIO
case 0x0f:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE MICKEY/PIXEL RATIO */

entries.name: set update region
entries.description: Defines a screen region where the cursor is not drawn.
entries.behaviour: CX,DX=upper left and SI,DI=lower right corner; redraws the cursor. Only text-mode drawing honours the region, and AX=0001h clears it. PC-98 NEC mouse mode: defines the horizontal range from CX and DX instead.
entries.differs: The list says the cursor is hidden inside the region in every mode; the emulator checks it only when drawing a text-mode cursor, the graphics-mode check is commented out.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE SCREEN REGION FOR UPDATING
case 0x10:  /* MS MOUSE v1.0+ - DEFINE SCREEN REGION FOR UPDATING */

entries.name: wheel support check
entries.description: Identifies the CuteMouse wheel extension; the list gives the Genius driver's button count.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=574Dh, BX=0 and CX=1 (wheel supported). PC-98 NEC mouse mode: defines the vertical range from CX and DX instead.
entries.differs: The list gives AX=FFFFh and the button count in BX; the emulator returns the CuteMouse wheel signature and no button count.

sources.cites: INT 33 - Genius Mouse 9.06 - GET NUMBER OF BUTTONS
case 0x11:  /* Genius Mouse 9.06 - GET NUMBER OF BUTTONS */

entries.name: large graphics cursor
entries.description: Sets a large graphics cursor block.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register. PC-98 NEC mouse mode: selects the drawing plane from BX.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=FFFFh on success; the emulator never changes AX, so it stays 0012h.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE - SET LARGE GRAPHICS CURSOR BLOCK
case 0x12:  /* MS MOUSE - SET LARGE GRAPHICS CURSOR BLOCK */

entries.name: double speed threshold
entries.description: Sets the speed above which the cursor motion is doubled.
entries.behaviour: DX=threshold, 0 becomes 64, is stored but never used: motion is not doubled. No register changes. PC-98 NEC mouse mode: returns BX=FFFFh (plane 3 available).

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v5.0+ - DEFINE DOUBLE-SPEED THRESHOLD
case 0x13:  /* MS MOUSE v5.0+ - DEFINE DOUBLE-SPEED THRESHOLD */

entries.name: exchange event handler
entries.description: Replaces the event routine and returns the previous one.
entries.behaviour: Stores CX, ES, DX as the new call mask, segment and offset and returns the previous ones in CX, ES, DX, without checks. Before any call the previous routine is segment 6362h, offset 0, and a reset clears the mask.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v3.0+ - EXCHANGE INTERRUPT SUBROUTINES
case 0x14:  /* MS MOUSE v3.0+ - EXCHANGE INTERRUPT SUBROUTINES */

entries.name: driver storage size
entries.description: Returns the size of the buffer needed to save the driver state.
entries.behaviour: BX=the size in bytes of the emulator's own driver state structure.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN DRIVER STORAGE REQUIREMENTS
case 0x15:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN DRIVER STORAGE REQUIREMENTS */

entries.name: save driver state
entries.description: Saves the driver state into a buffer.
entries.behaviour: Copies the whole driver state structure (the size AX=0015h reports) to ES:DX. BX is not read. The structure includes host pointers to the cursor masks.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SAVE DRIVER STATE
case 0x16:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SAVE DRIVER STATE */

entries.name: restore driver state
entries.description: Restores the driver state from a buffer saved earlier.
entries.behaviour: Overwrites the whole driver state structure with bytes from ES:DX, with no check of BX or of the contents. The structure includes host pointers to the cursor masks.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RESTORE DRIVER STATE
case 0x17:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RESTORE DRIVER STATE */

entries.name: set alt event handler
entries.description: Installs an event routine selected by shift-key states in its call mask.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error, stores nothing and changes no register.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0018h on success and FFFFh on error; the emulator leaves AX at 0018h without storing the handler.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET ALTERNATE MOUSE USER HANDLER
case 0x18:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET ALTERNATE MOUSE USER HANDLER */

entries.name: get alt event handler
entries.description: Returns the alternate event routine whose call mask matches CX.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so CX, BX and DX come back as passed.
entries.differs: The list returns the routine in BX:DX and CX=0000h if none matches; the emulator returns the registers unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN USER ALTERNATE INTERRUPT VECTOR
case 0x19:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN USER ALTERNATE INTERRUPT VECTOR */

entries.name: set sensitivity
entries.description: Sets the mouse sensitivity and double-speed threshold.
entries.behaviour: BX,CX,DX=horizontal speed, vertical speed, threshold, each capped at 100 and stored. Cursor motion is rescaled when BX and CX are both nonzero; the threshold has no effect. The startup value is 50,50,50.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET MOUSE SENSITIVITY
case 0x1a:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET MOUSE SENSITIVITY */

entries.name: get sensitivity
entries.description: Returns the mouse sensitivity and double-speed threshold.
entries.behaviour: BX,CX,DX=the horizontal speed, vertical speed and threshold last stored by AX=001Ah, already capped at 100; 50,50,50 after startup.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN MOUSE SENSITIVITY
case 0x1b:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN MOUSE SENSITIVITY */

entries.name: set interrupt rate
entries.description: Sets the mouse interrupt rate.
entries.behaviour: Does nothing: the rate is decided by the host, BX is ignored and no register changes.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET INTERRUPT RATE
case 0x1c:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET INTERRUPT RATE */

entries.name: set display page
entries.description: Sets the display page on which the cursor is drawn.
entries.behaviour: BL=page, stored; graphics-mode drawing and erasing use it, text modes use the BIOS current page. A reset sets 0. No register changes.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - DEFINE DISPLAY PAGE NUMBER
case 0x1d:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - DEFINE DISPLAY PAGE NUMBER */

entries.name: get display page
entries.description: Returns the display page on which the cursor is drawn.
entries.behaviour: BX=the page stored by AX=001Dh, 0 after a reset.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN DISPLAY PAGE NUMBER
case 0x1e:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - RETURN DISPLAY PAGE NUMBER */

entries.name: disable driver
entries.description: Disables the mouse driver and hides the cursor.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX=0 and ES=0 (no previous vector is given); AX stays 001Fh. Saves the hide counter and sets it to 1. Only the enabled flag that AX=0026h reports is cleared: events and position tracking go on.
entries.differs: The list returns the INT 33h vector from before the driver was installed in ES:BX; the emulator returns 0000h:0000h.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - DISABLE MOUSE DRIVER
case 0x1f:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - DISABLE MOUSE DRIVER */

entries.name: enable driver
entries.description: Enables the mouse driver again after AX=001Fh.
entries.behaviour: Sets the enabled flag and restores the hide counter saved by AX=001Fh (the saved value is 1 after a reset or mode set). AX stays 0020h and no other register changes.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - ENABLE MOUSE DRIVER
case 0x20:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - ENABLE MOUSE DRIVER */

entries.name: software reset
entries.description: Resets the driver state and reports whether it is installed, without resetting the hardware.
entries.behaviour: Same as AX=0000h minus the hardware reset: AX=FFFFh, BX=3 and the same reinitialisation. If the built-in driver was switched off (MOUSE /U) AX stays 0021h and nothing resets.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SOFTWARE RESET
case 0x21:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SOFTWARE RESET */

entries.name: set language
entries.description: Sets the language for the driver's messages.
entries.behaviour: BX=language, stored unchecked; AX=0023h returns it and a reset sets 0. No register changes.
entries.differs: The list says US versions ignore the call; the emulator always stores BX.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET LANGUAGE FOR MESSAGES
case 0x22:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - SET LANGUAGE FOR MESSAGES */

entries.name: get language
entries.description: Returns the language for the driver's messages.
entries.behaviour: BX=the language stored by AX=0022h, 0 after a reset.
entries.differs: The list says the US version always returns zero; the emulator returns what was stored.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.0+ - GET LANGUAGE FOR MESSAGES
case 0x23:  /* MS MOUSE v6.0+ - GET LANGUAGE FOR MESSAGES */

entries.name: get version and type
entries.description: Returns the driver version, the mouse type and its IRQ.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX=0805h (version 8.05), CH=4 (PS/2 type), CL=0 (PS/2 interrupt); AX stays 0024h and the input BX is not read. The values are fixed: they do not follow the configured mouse type.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET SOFTWARE VERSION, MOUSE TYPE, AND IRQ NUMBER
case 0x24:  /* MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET SOFTWARE VERSION, MOUSE TYPE, AND IRQ NUMBER */

entries.name: get driver info
entries.description: Returns general driver information such as the cursor type and the driver kind.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=1 (a guess noted in the code), AH=40h (integrated) combined with the cursor type shifted left 4 (0 software text, 1 hardware text, 2 graphics) and 01h (30 reports per second), BX=CX=DX=0. Bit 15 is never set.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET GENERAL DRIVER INFORMATION
case 0x25:  /* MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET GENERAL DRIVER INFORMATION */

entries.name: get max coordinates
entries.description: Returns the mouse-disabled flag and the maximum virtual coordinates.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX=0000h if enabled or FFFFh after AX=001Fh, CX=maximum x and DX=maximum y as currently set by AX=0007h and 0008h. After a reset the defaults depend on the video mode (graphics x 639, text columns times 8 minus 1).
entries.differs: The list says v7.05+ returns the absolute maximum; the emulator returns the maximum currently set, which the list gives for drivers before 7.05.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET MAXIMUM VIRTUAL COORDINATES
case 0x26:  /* MS MOUSE v6.26+ - GET MAXIMUM VIRTUAL COORDINATES */

entries.name: get masks and mickeys
entries.description: Returns the text cursor masks and the mickey counts.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=text screen mask and BX=text cursor mask (CX and DX of the last AX=000Ah, default 77FFh and 7700h), and CX,DX=mickeys as AX=000Bh (zero unless the host mouse is captured), then clears the counters.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.01+ - GET SCREEN/CURSOR MASKS AND MICKEY COUNTS
case 0x27:  /* MS MOUSE v7.01+ - GET SCREEN/CURSOR MASKS AND MICKEY COUNTS */

entries.name: set video mode
entries.description: Sets the video mode used by the mouse driver.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so no mode is set and CL keeps the low byte of the requested mode instead of a status.
entries.differs: The list returns CL=00h on success; the emulator leaves CL as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.0+ - SET VIDEO MODE
case 0x28:  /* MS MOUSE v7.0+ - SET VIDEO MODE */

entries.name: enumerate video modes
entries.description: Enumerates the video modes the mouse driver supports.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so CX and DS:DX come back as passed and nothing is enumerated.
entries.differs: The list returns the next mode in CX and a description at DS:DX; the emulator returns both unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.0+ - ENUMERATE VIDEO MODES
case 0x29: /* MS MOUSE v7.0+ - ENUMERATE VIDEO MODES */

entries.name: get cursor hot spot
entries.description: Returns the cursor visibility counter, hot spot and mouse type.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=the hide counter as a negative byte (0 visible, FFh hidden once), BX=hot spot column, CX=hot spot row, DX=4 (PS/2 mouse). AH is not modified.
entries.differs: The list returns the visibility counter in AX; the emulator sets only AL and leaves AH as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.02+ - GET CURSOR HOT SPOT
case 0x2a:  /* MS MOUSE v7.02+ - GET CURSOR HOT SPOT */

entries.name: load accel profiles
entries.description: Loads the mouse acceleration profiles.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so AX stays 002Bh and no profile is stored.
entries.differs: The list returns a success flag in AX; the emulator leaves AX unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.0+ - LOAD ACCELERATION PROFILES
case 0x2b:  /* MS MOUSE v7.0+ - LOAD ACCELERATION PROFILES */

entries.name: get accel profiles
entries.description: Returns the mouse acceleration profiles.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so AX, BX and ES:SI come back as passed.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h, the active profile in BX and a buffer at ES:SI; the emulator returns the registers unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.0+ - GET ACCELERATION PROFILES
case 0x2c:  /* MS MOUSE v7.0+ - GET ACCELERATION PROFILES */

entries.name: select accel profile
entries.description: Selects or reads the active mouse acceleration profile.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so AX stays 002Dh, which is neither the 0000h nor the FFFEh the list gives.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h or FFFEh with the profile name at ES:SI; the emulator returns the registers unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.0+ - SELECT ACCELERATION PROFILE
case 0x2d:  /* MS MOUSE v7.0+ - SELECT ACCELERATION PROFILE */

entries.name: set accel profile names
entries.description: Sets the names of the acceleration profiles.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so no names are stored and the ES:SI buffer is not filled.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h and fills the buffer when BL is nonzero; the emulator changes nothing.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v8.10+ - SET ACCELERATION PROFILE NAMES
case 0x2e:  /* MS MOUSE v8.10+ - SET ACCELERATION PROFILE NAMES */

entries.name: mouse hardware reset
entries.description: Resets the mouse hardware.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error, resets nothing and changes no register, so AX stays 002Fh.
entries.differs: The list returns a status in AX; the emulator leaves AX unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.02+ - MOUSE HARDWARE RESET
case 0x2f:  /* MS MOUSE v7.02+ - MOUSE HARDWARE RESET */

entries.name: ballpoint info
entries.description: Gets or sets BallPoint mouse information.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so AX stays 0030h.
entries.differs: The list returns FFFFh in AX when no BallPoint is present; the emulator leaves AX as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.04+ - GET/SET BallPoint INFORMATION
case 0x30:  /* MS MOUSE v7.04+ - GET/SET BallPoint INFORMATION */

entries.name: get min max coordinates
entries.description: Returns the current minimum and maximum virtual coordinates.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX=minimum x, BX=minimum y, CX=maximum x, DX=maximum y, as set by AX=0007h and 0008h or the video-mode defaults of the last reset.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET CURRENT MINIMUM/MAXIMUM VIRTUAL COORDINATES
case 0x31:  /* MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET CURRENT MINIMUM/MAXIMUM VIRTUAL COORDINATES */

entries.name: get active functions
entries.description: Returns the flags of the advanced functions the driver supports.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so AX stays 0032h and no flags are returned.
entries.differs: The list returns the function flags in AX and BX, CX, DX; the emulator leaves all of them as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET ACTIVE ADVANCED FUNCTIONS
case 0x32:  /* MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET ACTIVE ADVANCED FUNCTIONS */

entries.name: get switch settings
entries.description: Returns the mouse settings and acceleration profile data.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so no buffer size is returned and ES:DX is not filled.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h and the size or the data in CX and ES:DX; the emulator leaves the registers as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET SWITCH SETTINGS AND ACCELERATION PROFILE DATA
case 0x33:  /* MS MOUSE v7.05+ - GET SWITCH SETTINGS AND ACCELERATION PROFILE DATA */

entries.name: get ini file name
entries.description: Returns the name of the driver's initialization file.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so no file name is returned at ES:DX.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h and the file name at ES:DX; the emulator leaves the registers as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v8.0+ - GET INITIALIZATION FILE
case 0x34:  /* MS MOUSE v8.0+ - GET INITIALIZATION FILE */

entries.name: lcd large pointer
entries.description: Gets or sets the large pointer settings for LCD screens.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so no settings are read or stored.
entries.differs: The list returns AX=0000h and, for BX=FFFFh, the settings in BX, CX, DX; the emulator leaves the registers as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE v8.10+ - LCD SCREEN LARGE POINTER SUPPORT
case 0x35:  /* MS MOUSE v8.10+ - LCD SCREEN LARGE POINTER SUPPORT */

entries.name: copyright string ptr
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the driver's copyright string.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so ES:DI is not set; AX=0024h gives the version.
entries.differs: The list returns ES:DI pointing at the copyright message; the emulator leaves ES:DI as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE - RETURN POINTER TO COPYRIGHT STRING
case 0x4d:  /* MS MOUSE - RETURN POINTER TO COPYRIGHT STRING */

entries.name: get version string
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the driver's version number.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: the emulator logs an error and changes no register, so ES:DI is not set; AX=0024h gives the version.
entries.differs: The list returns ES:DI pointing at the major and BCD minor version; the emulator leaves ES:DI as passed.

sources.cites: INT 33 - MS MOUSE - GET VERSION STRING
case 0x6d:  /* MS MOUSE - GET VERSION STRING */

entries.name: logitech cyberman
entries.description: Logitech CyberMan 3D controller call, which the list has no section for.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs that the call is ignored by the regular mouse driver and changes no register.

sources.cites: case 0x53C1:  /* Logitech CyberMan */
